question.problem: Find the projection of the intersection between the ellipsoid $\frac{2(x-4)^{2}}{3}+\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{9}+\frac{{z}^{2}}{3}=1$ and the plane $2x-z=8$ onto the $xy$-plane.
question.worked_solution:
Since we want to find the projection onto the $xy$-plane, we need to eliminate the variable $z.$ First, we solve the equation of the plane for $z$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-z & =8\,⟹\,z=2x-8\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the expression for $z$ into the equation of the ellipsoid, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2(x-4)^{2}}{3}+\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{9}+\frac{(2x-8)^{2}}{3} & =1 \\ \frac{2(x-4)^{2}}{3}+\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{9}+\frac{(2(x-4))^{2}}{3} & =1 \\ \frac{2(x-4)^{2}}{3}+\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{9}+\frac{4(x-4)^{2}}{3} & =1 \\ 2(x-4)^{2}+\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{9} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-4)^{2}}{1/2}+\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{9} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the projection of the intersection is the ellipse $\frac{(x-4)^{2}}{1/2}+\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{9}=1.$
